correctness.rationale: For every odd p, Legendre reduces the valuation of a(n,k) to a sum over prime powers q of counts in the 2k-term interval minus floor(k/q). Each term is nonnegative, and each power q dividing one of n-1,n,n+1,n+2 contributes at least one to every even-k coefficient. Four consecutive central integers contain two multiples of 3 exactly for n=1 mod 3, but never two multiples of a prime power at least five or nine. The coefficient k=2 attains every remaining odd-prime bound, and k=4 attains the exceptional 3-bound. An even power-of-two degree k yields an odd coefficient by Lucas, so v2(gcd)=0. This proves the exact all-n formula, including n=2,3,4 and without extrapolating finite checks; CHECK.py independently passed 34000 assertions.

originality.rationale: The earliest inspected same-object archival paper, Han–Seo (2004, arxiv:math/0406378), supplies the Bessel coefficients but treats inverse relations and log concavity. Yang–Zheng (2013) supplies polynomial determinant structure. The publicly available OEIS A001498 is a coefficient table, not an all-n parity-filtered content theorem. MathOverflow 503276 (2025) proves only unfiltered row-index parity divisibility and does not determine even-degree gcds; the n=7 even-degree content is 63 rather than the cited common factor 7. Published nearby repository results involve other arrays and do not logically imply the Bessel formula. No equivalent or stronger covering theorem was identified, but inaccessible Carlitz/Grosswald literature could contain an unlocated equivalent; priority is qualified.

value.rationale: The even projection (y_n(X)+y_n(-X))/2-1 is a canonical algebraic operation, not an arbitrary slice. Its coefficient content is a natural exact invariant for the classical Bessel polynomial and has a complete all-index prime-power classification. The unique 3-adic defect, sharp in degree four, distinguishes it from the first retained coefficient and from known full-row divisibility; the four-consecutive-factor mechanism explains this structural boundary rather than merely tabulating gcds.
